visualReview.notes: Actually inspected all 13 final portable views and all 51 current renders. The geographic authoring label was then corrected from draft to preview without changing any source/runtime/detail model bytes; all 26 portable/shared image hashes remained identical, and all 25 refreshed medium-fi views were inspected again. Compared with four individually viewed local originals and all 78 reference contact views. East facade has the distinct 3:7:3:7:3 bay rhythm, three pedimented pavilions, tall Corinthian orders, rusticated ground, mezzanines, divided sash windows, actual carriage passages, continuous first-floor balustrade and ceremonial balcony. Warm garden front has a circular five-window bow, engaged columns, oval blind panels, shallow green copper half dome, attic/frieze, giant-column pavilions, own raised terrace and temple conservatory. Real open Ambassadors’ Court porch and attached palace masses retain their own plan. First-pass repairs removed stone channels crossing gateways, overlapping mezzanine/arch holes, hidden distant glazing, unsupported columns, incorrectly solid porch massing, misplaced porch orientation and excessive curve simplification. Fine sculpture and unseen facade details remain conservative interpretations.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Actually inspected all 13 final shared-material views, including native footprint placement. Seven authored groups and four shared limestone, plain concrete, painted metal and copper identities; six groups at street detail. Replaced the overly weathered ancient-stone finish with the catalog’s pale large-block limestone. Authored pale east and warm Bath-stone vertex colors preserve facade differences. Opaque grey-green glazing, slate/lead roofs, green copper and original geometric ornament use no photographic textures. Open porch, carriage gates, balconies and courtyard voids retain actual depth. Synthetic library ground exposes buried foundations intentionally; independent terrain is checked separately.

mediumFiReview.notes: Actually inspected all 25 current version-2 lighting, quality, silhouette, detail and forced-level views. Canonical palace asset and selected detail identities verify in every frame. Four explicit 993/3993/15844/63641 triangle levels meet their budgets. Skyline preserves the palace/courtyard plan, east three-pediment rhythm, garden bow, attached wings and open temple porch while flattening facade windows and omitting small relief. District restores major orders, balcony/parapet counters, openings and warm garden massing. Street restores true east/garden window recesses, full carriage passages, columns/support plinths, steps and finer roof edges; less-visible wing glazing remains simpler. Close adds turned balusters, capital leaves/fluting, fine sash bars, original pediment/frieze relief and thin courtyard paving. Corrected curve simplification now bounds the complete original vertex chain. Error budgets remain authoring estimates, not scan-derived measurements. Procedural neighbors are context only.

paving.notes: All 1316 actual-runtime paving triangle centroids remain above unchanged native ground. Exact three-courtyard coverage; no large floor triangles clipping the terrain. Paving is a thin interpreted building surface, not a surveyed threshold.

geographicReview.notes: Own connected palace outline 52776563341652 and 19 native component parts retain three courtyard voids; separate Royal Mews/Riding School, memorial, gates and detached neighbors are excluded. +X runs north-west along the east frontage and +Z north-east toward the Mall. Own native east range is about 107.9 m wide; owner nominal controls are 108 m frontage,120 m quadrangle-inclusive depth and 24 m main height. Projections and attached wings are retained beyond the nominal rectangle. Four full local originals plus primary owner/heritage descriptions establish the two principal fronts and southern court; aerial pixel capture was unavailable and is not claimed. Original 6 m native porch projection is interpreted as an open colonnade: its low body wall is recessed, with a separate buried platform/free columns/pitched temple roof and steps occupying the projection. Native evidence is preserved unchanged. Four original Terrarium tiles precede geometry; all 37249 samples, source hashes, datum and PNG 16 round trip verify. Native outlines span about−1.174..+0.470 m relative to the 6.4092 m dry eastern datum. Buried−4 m foundations and own terraces close sampled authored perimeters; host ground is unchanged. Source curvature simplification is bounded and measured above, with the open-porch interpretation separate. All actual visible garden/porch tread checks pass. Thin 3 m courtyard paving covers the exact three native courtyard areas and clears independent ground at all 1316 runtime triangle centroids. Terrain/contact engineering is approximate. Bounded preview; footprint replacement disabled.

The mapped quadrangle is retained; garden elevation, interior courts, hidden roofs, heraldic carving and exact gates remain medium-fi estimates. Previously used attribution/private imagery is excluded from this current review.

geometryValidation.notes: Source regeneration/import, strict detail-level and medium-fi audits, source/scene/terrain/placement schemas, actual asset inspection, matching repeated 30-tick states, six runtime-pack members and default preview query pass. All 51 current renders actually inspected;25 canonical medium-fi frame identities verify. Four original tile hashes, all 37249 independent samples, datum and PNG 16 round trip verify. limitations: Four local originals individually inspected; all 78 candidate contact views inspected. Many candidates are interiors, a Shenzhen replica, nearby landmarks, gates, vehicles or historical images and cannot control the palace exterior.

Nominal 108m frontage, 120m quadrangle depth and 24m height are primary owner controls. Native front is approximately 107.9m wide; projections, attached south blocks and conservatories extend beyond the nominal main rectangle. Preserve native outlines rather than scaling the parcel to these numbers.

Main palace quadrangle, garden bow, attached conservatory/ballroom and Ambassadors’ Court masses only. Separate Royal Mews and Riding School, forecourt gates, Victoria Memorial, gardens, neighbors, interiors, people, guards, vehicles, temporary works/canopies, banners and photographic textures are excluded.
Qualla narrative dates the balcony to the 1913 refacing; owner records place its introduction with the 1847–1849 wing and appearances from 1851. Story content is not changed by this modeling work.

Native generalized component heights of 6/12/18/21/24m are massing evidence, not surveyed storey levels. Intermediate heights, unseen facade bays, stone detailing, roof engineering and flagstaff dimensions require conservative interpretation.
The owner aerial page was located and the image opened, but browser pixel capture failed. No aerial imagery has been visually inspected for this model yet.
Independent original terrain must be acquired before authoring. No terrain fitting/flattening or footprint replacement. Ground contacts and raised terraces must be tested against the actual samples.

The native6m Ambassadors’ Court porch projection is interpreted as an open colonnade, with its solid low wall recessed behind real columns and a pitched temple roof. Original footprints remain preserved. This changes the authored mass partition, not the host terrain or map evidence.
